title: Samsara re-read through recreation
statement: The canon re-reads the rebirth cycle of the Dharmic traditions through its recreation mechanism: in the second message Yahweh takes the Buddhist frame and renders the cycle scientifically — recreation from preserved records rather than metaphysical transmigration — so that samsara joins resurrection (woh-claim-0029) among the religious structures the canon demystifies into the same technology; the mapping preserves the traditions' irreducible differences as the comparative discipline requires.

includes: The canonical re-reading: the rebirth cycle rendered as recreation, delivered in the second message's engagement with the Buddhist frame
The pairing with woh-claim-0029: one mechanism behind two re-described structures (resurrection; rebirth), which is itself part of the canon's religion-of-religions posture (woh-claim-0027)
The preservation clause: Hindu, Buddhist, Jain, and Sikh articulations of the cycle differ irreducibly (karma theory, anatta, liberation goals), and the mapping does not flatten them
excludes: Karma theory as content; the canon's re-reading concerns the cycle's mechanism, not the moral accounting
Any claim that the Dharmic traditions' own soteriology anticipates the technology; the mapping is the canon's, stated as such
Liberation (moksha, nirvana) re-description, which the canon does not perform and the corpus does not invent
The identity metaphysics, registered and unresolved in woh-claim-0029

source_references.locator: The second message's Buddhist-frame engagement and the scientific rendering of the cycle
TBWTT-5:54 (Buddhism among the enumerated testifying traditions)

alternatives.statement: Rendering transmigration as recreation re-describes a soteriological structure in technological idiom — the standing critique at its clearest application.
Anatta makes 'the same being recreated' precisely what Buddhist philosophy denies; the mapping fits the frame it borrows worse than any other.

revision_triggers: Claim woh-claim-0001 or woh-claim-0029 is revised or retired.
The canon's fuller context changes the re-reading.
Public prose begins re-describing liberation or flattening the traditions, both of which this record excludes.
